### 1. What the user expresses, and how the simulator behaves

- Object: "I want to pay this car loan off in full today" — the Honda he financed with the bank.
- Timing: today, on this call — "he wants it done on this call, not quoted for some later date; he says so if he is asked whether he wants a figure for today or for a future date."
- Boundary: "He is happy for the representative to make whatever entries the bank's rules require on the loan first."
- Authorisation: "he says he will give any instruction that has to come from him personally while he is on the line"; the money comes "from an account he keeps at another bank", and "he is content for the representative to take that money and post it to the loan for him."

The simulator is passive: identity facts only on request (`3365550588`, `1968-11-30`, `1562`, `27405`); he admits being behind but offers no figures — "Whatever the payoff is, tell me the number and I'll send it"; he agrees to the coverage close-out only if the agent raises it — "If the representative explains that the protection product financed with the loan has to be closed out first … he says, 'That's fine by me'" — and "if the representative never mentions the protection product he does not mention it either." He runs the user-owned tool handed to him for the figure he is told and reads the confirmation back.

### 4. Each scored parameter, in words, with its inputs and tier

Derived readings:

- Loan seasoning: funded 2024-02-09 to 2026-09-16 = **31 whole months**.
- Checking account age: opened 2021-05-20 to 2026-09-16 = **63 whole months**.
- The two Personal Checking readings: posted balance 3167.25 against the fee-waiver daily balance published for the **Premier Checking** tier — `docs/checking/maintenance_fee_and_waiver_settings_3fe43226`, "Lowest end-of-day balance in the cycle (USD) | Premier Checking | 10000.00" — **fails**; recurring deposits posted in the last three months = 3 — **holds**. So **exactly one of the two holds**.
- Card purchases over the last twelve months = **6950.00 USD** (11 purchases 2025-11-08 … 2026-09-11). Card purchases posted in the last three months = **7**. Unredeemed reward points = **9800**.
- Scheduled installments credited to the loan in the last twelve months = **9** (2025-10-14 … 2026-06-14).
- Charge financed at funding: `auto_payoff_waiver_and_title_parameters_201390f0`, "One-time waiver charge financed at funding, USD | New Vehicle Loan | 795.00", which matches `gap_premium 795.00` on the loan.

**(a) The refund owed on the waiver coverage.**

`auto_waiver_refund_measurement_095de383`: "the unearned part of the charge financed at funding, less the cancellation fee … The unearned part is the refundable share of the charge financed at funding, multiplied by the months remaining and divided by the term the loan was written for."

- Refundable share — `auto_waiver_refundable_share_68da3bed`, "At least 8 but fewer than 12 | 95 percent"; 9 installments credited in the last twelve months → **95 %**; 95 % of 795.00 = **755.25**.
- Months remaining — `auto_waiver_refund_months_remaining_f2778f49`, "Where exactly one of those two holds, the months remaining are counted from the installment then due to the scheduled maturity"; installment then due 2026-07-15, maturity 2029-02-15 → **31 months**.
- Basis of the unearned part — `auto_waiver_unearned_part_convention_2f732def`, "**Opened at least 48 but less than 120 whole months before the cancellation:** the months remaining are taken up to the whole quarter above before the share is worked out"; 63 months → 31 taken up to **33**.
- Unearned part = 755.25 × 33 ⁄ 60 = **415.3875**.
- Cancellation fee — `auto_waiver_cancellation_fee_steps_2c5967c0`, middle row (9800 ≥ 5000, 7 ≥ 3, points short of 25000 and purchases short of 12) → **25.00**; 415.3875 − 25.00 = **390.3875**.
- Rounding — `auto_waiver_refund_rounding_f5742ffd`, "at least 24 but less than 36 whole months … rounded half-up to the whole dollar"; 31 months → **390.00**.
- The refund is entered against the loan, not paid out: "It is entered against the loan rather than paid out to the borrower, so the loan's unpaid principal falls by it." Principal 20443.37 → **20053.37**.

**(b) The amount required to settle the loan in full.**

`auto_settlement_amount_measurement_ab472e6b`: "the unpaid principal the loan's records then show, together with the interest owed for the days the settlement clock runs and the charges standing unpaid on the loan, added and rounded half-up to the cent … The settlement clock runs for the days the anchor gives together with the transit allowance."

- Clock anchor — `auto_settlement_clock_anchor_7ec5f95f`, "Where exactly one of those two holds, the clock runs from the date the installment then due falls on" → **2026-07-15**; span to 2026-09-16 = **63 days** (which is also what `days_past_due 63` reads).
- Transit allowance — `auto_settlement_transit_allowance_d756331b`, "**1 day** where that card carries at least 5000 unredeemed reward points and at least 3 card purchases have posted in the last three months, while either those points fall short of 25000 or those purchases fall short of 12" → **1 day**. Clock runs **64 days**.
- Settlement rate — `auto_settlement_rate_steps_bce3a86e`, middle row (6950.00 ≥ 3000.00, 9 ≥ 8, purchases short of 12000.00 and installments short of 12) → "The rate recorded on the loan, less the automatic-payment reduction the product publishes" = 6.24 − 0.25 (`auto_rate_sheet_and_reductions_35408558`, New Vehicle Loan) = **5.99 %**.
- Interest = 20053.37 × 5.99 ⁄ 100 ⁄ 365 × 64 = 210.6208…; rounding — `auto_settlement_interest_rounding_df3b0031`, 31 months → half-up to the whole dollar → **211.00**.
- Charges standing unpaid = **44.00** (the two late charges of 22.00; `auto_late_charge_state_basis_10b2fd7d`, "Late charges are recorded among the unpaid charges on the loan and are paid first out of later payments").
- Settlement = 20053.37 + 211.00 + 44.00 = **20308.37**.

### 6. The problem tree derived from the visible materials alone

**Problems, direction, order.** Two problems, handled 1 → 2. The dependency points backwards: the settlement of the loan waits on the refund owed on the waiver coverage standing entered on the loan's records.

**Hop A — the settlement waits on the coverage refund being entered. `state-derived`.**
Visible sentence, in the blocked problem's own hub `auto_loan_settlement_postings_ad938755`: "**The amount required to settle the loan in full is fixed only after the refund owed on the waiver coverage financed with the loan stands entered on its records.** Where the loan's records carry no such refund entry, or still show that coverage as in force, the amount required to settle the loan is not yet fixed."
Query returns: `find_auto_loans` → `gap_coverage True`, `gap_premium 795.00`, `gap_cancellation_date ''`; `find_auto_transactions` → 31 rows, none of them a refund entry. Both limbs of the waited-on state fail.
Finding the write that brings it about: the sentence's own words are "the refund owed on the waiver coverage financed with the loan" standing "entered on its records". `KB_search "cancelling GAP coverage on an auto loan"` returns `auto_waiver_coverage_cancellation_terms_ed709618` first — "The borrower may cancel it at any time while the loan is open. Cancelling is the borrower's own decision: it is recorded through a cancellation request of the borrower's own, which the borrower confirms" — and `auto_waiver_coverage_closeout_entries_e226ce80` second, which describes the write itself: "the cancellation is recorded, the coverage ends, and the refund owed on it is entered against the loan, so the loan's unpaid principal falls by that sum." Nothing told me to call anything; the state named in the sentence, the record showing it absent, and the depended-on documents' own rule supplied the hop.

**No hop was pre-solved.** The hub sentence names a record-visible state and nothing else — no tool, no policy id, no order across a chain. `post_gap_refund_16f4decd` occurs in exactly one document, its own hub, and `post_loan_payoff_a84c6454` likewise.

**A trap the corpus closes rather than opens.** `auto_waiver_coverage_cancellation_terms_ed709618` marks four bases retired, the fourth being: "The basis by which paying the loan off early while the coverage was in force was of itself treated as a cancellation dated on the payoff date is no longer in force." Had that still been in force, the payoff alone would have carried the cancellation and the tree would collapse to one problem. Its retirement is what makes the hop load-bearing, and it is stated as retired, not as a rule.

### Two-way counter-proof

**The conclusion is fully supported.** Every figure rests on a quoted sentence and a query return.

**The closest alternatives are excluded by visible sentences or records:**

- *Quote a payoff for a future date rather than settle today.* `auto_payoff_quotes_and_lien_release_bb226c70` A.1 allows a quote "for a date up to the number of calendar days ahead that the product publishes"; the borrower rules it out — "he wants it done on this call, not quoted for some later date" — and C.1 governs the payment that settles.
- *Work the interest at the rate recorded on the loan.* Closed by `auto_settlement_rate_steps_bce3a86e`: the borrower's readings put him on the middle row, so the settlement rate is 5.99 %, not the recorded 6.24 %.
- *Start the settlement clock at `last_payment_date` 2026-06-14.* Closed by `auto_settlement_clock_anchor_7ec5f95f`: that anchor is the "neither of them holds" row, and exactly one holds here, so the clock starts at the installment date 2026-07-15.
- *Pay the refund out to the borrower or to his checking account.* Closed twice: `auto_waiver_refund_measurement_095de383` — "It is entered against the loan rather than paid out to the borrower" — and the retired third basis in `auto_waiver_coverage_cancellation_terms_ed709618`.
- *Refund the whole 795.00 charge.* Closed: that was the retired first basis, and in any event this loan funded 31 months ago, far outside the 60-calendar-day full-refund window `auto_payoff_waiver_and_title_parameters_201390f0` publishes.
- *Waive the two late charges before settling.* `auto_fee_waiver_grounds_1da01371` gives only bank error and courtesy; nothing in the records shows the charges were assessed contrary to the charter — North Carolina publishes 15 grace days (`auto_fee_schedule_and_state_annex_5cb062b4`) and each charge is dated the sixteenth day after its own installment, 2026-07-31 against 2026-07-15 and 2026-08-31 against 2026-08-15, one per installment as 4.1 requires — and the courtesy ground fails its consecutive-on-time-installments condition on a loan 63 days past due with two consecutive late installments. The borrower asks for no waiver.
- *Grant an extension or arrange something on the delinquency.* `auto_payment_extension_terms_4aee01c7` and `auto_delinquency_and_charge_off_5a62ce69` both put such matters outside themselves, and the borrower asks to pay in full.
- *One boundary the source leaves open, recorded as a policy-side note:* `auto_payoff_quotes_and_lien_release_bb226c70` A.2 remains in force and gives a per-diem worked at "the rate recorded on the loan", which is 6.24 % and not the 5.99 % settlement rate. A.2 is scoped to a payoff **quote**, and B.1 retires the basis on which the amount itself was measured and sends the reader to the basis now in force; a reader who nevertheless carried A.2's rate into the settlement would reach a different figure. Flagged for the reveal as a possible second in-force basis rather than a rendering defect.

**The wrong answer "he asked for one thing, so do one thing" is excluded by reasoning, not by a pointer.** Calling `post_loan_payoff_a84c6454` alone leaves the governed result in a state the visible principles do not allow: the hub's own sentence says that while the records "still show that coverage as in force, the amount required to settle the loan is not yet fixed", and the record reads `gap_coverage True` with no refund entry — so the figure passed would not be the amount required, and `auto_waiver_coverage_cancellation_terms_ed709618` expressly retires the basis that would otherwise have let the payoff carry the cancellation. Nor could the agent cancel it himself: cancelling "is the borrower's own decision … which the borrower confirms."

| Refund owed on the coverage | refundable share 90 % of 795.00 = 715.50; months remaining 60 − 31 = 29; 715.50 × 29 ⁄ 60 = 345.825; less the published 50.00 cancellation fee; half-up to the cent → **295.83** | **390.00** |
| Amount required to settle in full | anchor `last_payment_date` 2026-06-14 (94 days) + transit allowance 3 = 97 days at the recorded 6.24 %; interest half-up to the cent = 332.55; 20053.37 + 332.55 + 44.00 → **20429.92** | **20308.37** |

- `auto_waiver_cancellation_fee_steps_2c5967c0`, `auto_settlement_transit_allowance_d756331b`: from `rewards_balance 9800` and the `card_purchase` rows on the Personal Credit Cards account.

- `KB_search "cancelling GAP coverage on an auto loan"` returns the measurement and three of its factor documents inside the first seven results; none of them was reached by guessing that a variation exists, and neither computation document hints that one does — `auto_waiver_refund_measurement_095de383` states "The refundable share is 90 percent of the charge financed at funding" flatly, and `auto_settlement_amount_measurement_ab472e6b` states "The transit allowance is 3 days" flatly.

The one-cent difference in the refund's baseline figure (295.83 against `baseline_result: 295.82`) is a rounding artefact of where the half-up to the cent is applied in the baseline chain; it is a figure neither side scores, and the scored `expected` of 390.00 agrees exactly.

The two boundaries flagged as open in the blind answer resolve as policy-side notes, not as document defects:

- `auto_payoff_quotes_and_lien_release_bb226c70` A.2's per-diem at "the rate recorded on the loan" comes from `auto_evt_payoff_and_lien.formula.per_diem`, which no `overwrite` supersedes. The KB carries an in-force base clause faithfully. It is scoped to a payoff quote, and `auto_ext_payoff_settlement` governs the amount required to settle; no second in-force basis for the settlement exists.
- The retired full-refund window basis in `auto_waiver_coverage_cancellation_terms_ed709618` corresponds to `auto_ext_gap_cancellation_refund.overwrite` on `auto_evt_gap_refund`, so the retirement is the source's own and is carried as retired.

### Verdict

Every scored figure the blind audit reached from the visible materials alone — 390.00, 20308.37, the split, the channel, and the two-problem tree with its single state-form edge and its order — equals the source layer's, with no divergence at all. No conclusion required hidden compute, GT or the raw `initial_state`. The prerequisite the source declares is carried verbatim on the blocked side, in its declared form, at the same strength. Every declared factor is entailed and reachable from the records. No tool schema, parameter, owner or effect disagrees with the source.

**PASS** (no `KB-RUNTIME RED`).
